newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech SPT Q1 revs rise but profit dips.
newsitem.headline: Czech SPT Q1 revs rise but profit dips.

text.p: Revenues at SPT Telecom a.s., the Czech Republic's main telephone operator, rose strongly in the first quarter, year-on-year, but depreciation and labour costs bit into the firm's bottom line.
SPT said in a statement on Wednesday that its revenues for the first three months rose to 9.04 billion crowns ($292.2 million) from 7.34 billion for the same period last year.

But, the statement added, net profit edged down to 1.59 billion from a previous 1.75 billion after depreciation charges rose some 34 percent to 1.83 billion crowns, and staff costs grew by 18 percent to 1.59 billion.
SPT did not comment on the figures in the statement, but analysts said they were positive even though the market itself did not react favourably.
"I am wondering why people perceived the first quarter results as worse than expected because on the operational level SPT is quite good," said INB Barings trader Radim Bajgar.
SPT shares dropped slightly on the Prague Stock Exchange following the results, closing down 35 crowns at 3,270.
The SPT statement did not say how many lines SPT had installed so far in 1997, but officials have said they hope to install some 450,000 new lines in 1997.
At the end of 1996, phone lines per employee were 108, but the number should rise to over 300 per employee by the year 2000 and projected revenues should rise by about 20 percent.
SPT's bottom line was hit hard in 1996, as it provisioned itself for large-scale layoffs in the coming years.

SPT plans to layoff some 5,000-6,000 employees through redundancies as it moves to digitalisation which is less labour intensive, with additional losses coming through attrition, currently at about 12 percent annually.
SPT is currently seeking a credit rating from Standard and Poor's, to give it "more borrowing flexibility", though no international bond issue for this year has yet been approved.
A consortium of Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV and Swiss Telecom bought a 27 percent stake in SPT last year from the Czech government for $1.32 billion plus $141 million in additional services.
